The '''2020–21 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Cincinnati]] in the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bearcats were led by second-year head-coach [[John Brannen (basketball)|John Brannen]]. The team played their home games at [[Fifth Third Arena]] as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 12–11, 8–6 in [[2020–21 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish in fifth place. They defeated [[2020–21 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]] and [[2020–21 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] in the [[2021 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] before losing to [[2020–21 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the championship game.

On April 3, 2021, the school placed head coach Brannen on paid leave pending an investigation after six Bearcats players decided to transfer following the season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-03|title=Cincinnati coach Brannen on leave amid inquiry|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31189472/cincinnati-coach-john-brannen-leave-amid-investigation|access-date=2021-04-12|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> A week later, the school fired Brannen following an investigation into his conduct.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-09|title=Cincy fires Brannen after investigation of program|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31223738/cincinnati-bearcats-fire-men-basketball-coach-john-brannen-following-investigation-program|access-date=2021-04-12|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Bearcats]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 20–10, 13–5 in [[2019–20 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]], finishing tied for first place and winning a share of the regular season title. The Cats kept fans on the edge of their seats with a nation-leading seven overtime games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://digital.learfieldimgcollege.com/cincinnati-mbb-review/full-view.html |title=Cincinnati Basketball Season Review by Learfield IMG College |access-date=2020-04-07 |archive-date=2020-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407050201/http://digital.learfieldimgcollege.com/cincinnati-mbb-review/full-view.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> They entered as the No. 1 seed in the [[2020 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], which was ultimately cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]]. The Bearcats were awarded the automatic bid to the [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] by the conference, before it too was cancelled.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2020/03/12/coronavirus-american-athletic-conference-cancels-tournament/5031589002/ |title=American Athletic Conference cancels men's basketball tournament amid coronavirus concerns |last=Page |first=Fletcher |date=12 Mar 2020 |work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|access-date=17 Apr 2020 }}</ref>

==Offseason==

==Schedule and results==
The Bearcats are currently scheduled to travel to Knoxville for the second part of a home-and-home series with Tennessee and begin a home-and-home series on the road at Georgia.  Cincinnati and Xavier announced they would maintain the [[Crosstown Shootout]] during the season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=WATCH: Cincinnati coach John Brannen reveals Crosstown Shootout vs. Xavier set for 2020-21 season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/watch-cincinnati-coach-john-brannen-reveals-crosstown-shootout-vs-xavier-set-for-2020-21-season/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=22 October 2020}}</ref>

===COVID-19 impact===
{{main|Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports}}

Due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the Bearcats schedule is subject to change, including the cancellation or postponement of individual games, the cancellation of the entire season, or games played either with minimal fans or without fans in attendance and just essential personnel.

*3 previously scheduled games were cancelled (vs. [[2020–21 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], vs. [[2020–21 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]], @ [[2020–21 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|NKU]]), as well as the Bearcats appearance in the [[NIT Season Tip-Off]] (alongside [[2020–21 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], [[2020–21 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] and [[2020–21 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=NIT Season Tip-Off 2020 Field Announced|url=https://espnevents.com/news-and-updates/nit-tip-off/2020-field-announced/|website=ESPN Events|publisher=ESPN|access-date=11 November 2019}}</ref> As a response to all these outcomes, UC attempted to organize an [[Indianapolis]]-based MTE alongside [[2020–21 Duquesne Dukes men's basketball team|Duquesne]] and [[2020–21 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola-Chicago]]. Ironically, that too would be cancelled due to COVID.<ref>{{cite tweet| last=Rothstein|first=Jon|user=JonRothstein|number=1329567191285571592|date=19 November 2020|title=Sources: This entire MTE is now off in Indianapolis. Original field was Cincinnati, Loyola-Chicago, and Duquesne.|link=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/1329567191285571592|accessdate=19 November 2020}}</ref>
*The games vs. [[2020–21 Temple Owls men's basketball team|Temple]] originally scheduled for February 4 was moved to Philadelphia.<ref>{{cite web |title=The American Announces Men's Basketball Schedule Changes |url=http://theamerican.org/news/2021/1/27/the-american-announces-mens-basketball-schedule-changes.aspx|date=27 Jan 2021}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the season, UC announced there would be no fans in Fifth Third Arena; only permitting fans in the arena later in the season if it's safe and appropriate to do so.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Jenkins |first1=Keith |title=Update: University of Cincinnati basketball hopes for 'limited' fans at Fifth Third Arena |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2020/11/03/cincinnati-basketball-no-fans-start-season-fifth-third-arena/6137415002/ |website=Enquirer.cin |publisher=Cincinnati Enquirer |access-date=13 November 2020}}</ref> UC was later granted an attendance variance by the State of [[Ohio]] which allows for crowds of around 1,135 fans inside the arena for games against Tulane (Feb. 26), Memphis (Feb. 28) and SMU, rescheduled as Vanderbilt, (March 4).<ref>{{cite web |title=Athletics Announces Increased Capacity At Fifth Third Arena |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2021/2/16/mens-basketball-athletics-announces-increased-capacity-at-fifth-third-arena.aspx|date=16 Feb 2021}}</ref>
